data.body: Phase 1 confirmed root cause: tests/_isolation.py runs both `git rev-parse HEAD` (`head`) and `git status --porcelain` (`porcelain`) synchronously with no timeout. A deterministic blocking-git experiment through the real `pytest_sessionfinish` hook kept nested pytest alive after `[100%]`; a captured live stack ended in `subprocess.run/_communicate -> tests/_isolation.py:porcelain -> tests/conftest.py:pytest_sessionfinish`, ruling out a still-running test, fixture body, and terminal progress rendering. The same missing bound is reachable through `_no_repo_commits` before/after each unmarked test. 100 normal repo-root status probes were median 0.0143s, p95 0.0164s, max 0.0610s, rejecting normal repo cost as the cause and leaving >80x headroom for the approved 5-second watchdog. Historical inspection shows both unbounded probes were introduced together in d8b077451b; no later timeout was removed. Important repair constraint: `TimeoutExpired` subclasses the currently caught `SubprocessError`, so adding only `timeout=5` would silently return `None`; timeout must be separated and surface as an explicit isolation-infrastructure failure while ordinary non-repo/launch/nonzero failures keep returning `None`. Legitimacy: defect, because the signed plan requires the fixed watchdog and explicit timeout failure, and the guard contract says checkout mutation must fail loudly. Caller sweep found only `_no_repo_commits`, session start/finish hooks, and their tests; none behaviorally depends on indefinite waiting or swallowed timeouts.
